comparison: Perfect agreement on nomenclature and etymology (C12, C13). Both evaluations find these claims supported as standard taxonomic practice.

Significant disagreement on functional interpretations (C51-C58, C98, C115, C118). OpenEval rates these as UNCERTAIN, noting the photosynthetic nutrition hypothesis is speculative and based on analogy rather than direct evidence. Peer reviewers fully SUPPORT these claims without raising concerns about the speculative nature.

Major disagreement on mathematical modeling (C71, C78-C93, C101, C121). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, identifying internal contradictions (three-winged claimed superior despite four-winged having higher calculated efficiency 90.03% vs 82.70%), lack of empirical validation, and overstated conclusions. Peer reviewers fully SUPPORT the analysis, describing it as 'solid mathematical analysis' and accepting the three-winged superiority claim without noting the contradiction.

Strong agreement on morphological descriptions (C18-C46). Both evaluations find the extensive morphological documentation well-supported by figures and measurements. OpenEval emphasizes quantitative data and structural observations; peer reviewers praise 'exceptionally well-preserved fossil specimens' and 'superb illustrations.'

Strong agreement on evolutionary narrative and comparative morphology (C59-C76, C99-C100, C107-C113, C119-C120). Both evaluations find the evolutionary sequence from Famennian winged ovules through Carboniferous to Permian seeds well-supported by fossil record and appropriate citations.

Agreement on rarity and significance of acupulate Famennian ovules (C47-C50, C94-C97). Both evaluations support the characterization of Alasemenia as the second such taxon and its paleobotanical significance.

Agreement on stratigraphic and geographic context (C1-C3, C10, C16-C17, C102). Both evaluations find geological context, age determination, and locality information well-documented and supported. Peer reviewers accept these claims without question.

Agreement on paleobotanical context (C4-C9). OpenEval finds the taxa descriptions and citations appropriate for Late Devonian floras. Peer reviewers implicitly accept this context as part of their overall positive assessment of the geological framework.

Agreement on methods (C103-C106). OpenEval finds preparation and documentation methods appropriate. Peer reviewers explicitly state 'The methods used in the manuscript are appropriate' and praise the illustrations.
